qidi_install.text: HelixScreen replaces QIDI's own screen program. While HelixScreen runs, QIDI Studio cannot see the QIDI Box or send prints to this printer, QIDI cloud is unavailable, and filament changes made for the Box do not stick. Prints can still be sent through Moonraker (Fluidd, Mainsail or a slicer's Klipper connection). Removing HelixScreen later brings all of this back.

k1_stock.text: If the printer's screen offers a firmware update, tap Cancel: the installer works with the firmware the printer has.

k1_stock.question: On the printer's screen, open Settings. Is there an entry called Root account information?

k1_stock.reason: This printer has no root option. Some 2025 K1C units ship without it, and the installer cannot put HelixScreen on them.

k1_stock.text: Before you start: the installer first puts Simple AF, a community firmware, on this printer, then HelixScreen. Going back to Creality's own software later takes a factory reset or Creality's recovery firmware; removing only HelixScreen is quick and leaves Simple AF's screen. Simple AF's installer turns off certificate checking for git on the printer, and it stays off.
Turn on root access: on the printer's screen open Settings, then Root account information. Read the notice, wait for the countdown, then press OK. Then press I've done this.

k1_stock.ssh: case "$(/usr/bin/get_sn_mac.sh model 2>/dev/null)" in CR-K1|K1C|"CR-K1 Max") echo yes;; *) echo no;; esac

k1_stock.reason: This installer supports the Creality K1, K1C and K1 Max only, and this printer says it is another model.
Simple AF needs Creality firmware 1.3.3.5 or newer. Update the printer from its own screen, then run the installer again.

k1_stock.ssh: if [ -d /usr/data/helper-script ] || [ -f /usr/data/fluidd.sh ] || [ -f /usr/data/mainsail.sh ] || { [ -d /opt ] && [ ! -L /opt ] && [ -n "$(ls -1 /opt)" ]; }; then echo yes; else echo no; fi

k1_stock.reason: Something from an earlier mod is on this printer (Helper Script, Creality's Fluidd or Mainsail script, or files in /opt). Simple AF installs only on a printer fresh from a factory reset. A factory reset erases what the earlier mod kept, its print files and print history included, so download any print files you want to keep first. Then reset the printer from its Settings and run the installer again.

k1_stock.command: git config --global http.sslVerify false; if [ -d /usr/data/pellcorp/.git ]; then git -C /usr/data/pellcorp remote get-url origin | grep -q 'github.com/pellcorp/creality' || { echo 'FATAL: /usr/data/pellcorp is not a copy of pellcorp/creality; factory reset the printer and start again'; exit 1; }; git -C /usr/data/pellcorp pull || { echo 'FATAL: could not update /usr/data/pellcorp (git pull failed); check the printer can reach github.com, then retry'; exit 1; }; elif [ -e /usr/data/pellcorp ]; then echo 'FATAL: /usr/data/pellcorp is in the way; factory reset the printer and start again'; exit 1; else git clone https://github.com/pellcorp/creality.git /usr/data/pellcorp; fi && sh /usr/data/pellcorp/k1/installer.sh --install loadcells

k1_stock.text: Simple AF has finished installing. Turn the printer off with its power switch, wait 10 seconds, then turn it back on: this updates the firmware on the printer's boards. Then press I've done this.

k1_restore.text: This removes HelixScreen and puts back the screen the printer had before it (GrumpyScreen on Simple AF, or the one your Helper Script setup used). Creality's own screen and software come back only with a factory reset or Creality's recovery firmware; the K1 guide explains both: https://helixscreen.org/guide/install-k1/

ad5x_zmod.text: Find the printer's firmware version: on its screen open Settings, then the About page. The installer asks for it next.

ad5x_zmod.question: Which firmware version does the About page show?

ad5x_zmod.reason: ZMOD installs only over stock firmware 1.1.7 to 1.2.3 (not 1.1.8), 3.0.3, 3.0.9 or 3.1.0. The AD5X guide explains how to put a supported version on first.

ad5x_zmod.text: ZMOD installs only on a printer reset to factory settings: its own guide makes this a requirement. A reset can erase the print files stored on the printer, so copy any you want to keep to your computer first. Reset the printer from its Settings now if it has not been reset since its firmware was last flashed. Then press Next to copy ZMOD onto a USB stick.
Turn the printer off, put the USB stick in the printer's USB port, then turn the printer on. It installs ZMOD by itself, which can take up to 40 minutes. Press I've done this once the printer is on.

ad5x_zmod.message: ZMOD is installing; this can take up to 40 minutes. Do not power off the printer. Remove the USB stick afterwards.
ad5x_zmod.help: If the printer's screen shows an error or stays on one message for a long time, follow the AD5X guide: https://helixscreen.org/guide/install-ad5x/

ad5x_zmod.text: Remove the USB stick from the printer now. Left in, it installs ZMOD again on the next start.

ad5m_forgex.text: Find the printer's firmware version: on its screen open Settings, then the About page. The installer asks for it next.

ad5m_forgex.question: Which firmware version does the About page show?

ad5m_forgex.reason: Forge-X installs over stock firmware 2.6.5 to 5.1.x. The AD5M guide explains how to get the printer onto one of those versions.

Firmware 3.1.5 can be missing the printer's configuration files: FlashForge's own 3.1.5 image does not include them, so a printer that was reset or wiped and then given that image has none, and Forge-X will not work on it. If this printer prints normally now, it has them and you can continue. If you are not sure, stop and flash FlashForge's Factory image first, then run the installer again.

ad5m_forgex.text: Turn the printer off, put the USB stick in the printer's USB port, then turn the printer on. It installs Forge-X by itself and shows a message on its screen when it has finished. Press I've done this once the printer is on.
When the printer's screen says the installation has finished, remove the USB stick and turn the printer off and on again. Then press I've done this.

ktouch_install.reason: This USB device is not a K-Touch: its chip is not an ESP32-S3, so the installer will not write to it.
This board does not have the K-Touch's 16 MB of flash, so the installer will not write to it.

ktouch_install.text: Installing HelixScreen removes everything on the K-Touch first: BigTreeTech's firmware, its WiFi and its settings. You set it up again on its own screen afterwards. Keep it plugged into this computer until the installer says it is done.

HelixScreen is on your K-Touch and it has restarted. Finish setting it up on the K-Touch's own screen. If it shows Set Up WiFi, join the HelixScreen network it names from your phone, open the address it shows, then choose your WiFi and enter your printer's address. If it joins your WiFi by itself, enter your printer's address in Settings > Connection > Host.
